stories.title: Gajanan Maharaj reveals his divine nature at Devidas's house in Shegaon

boundary_evidence.reason: Author explicitly begins the story: 'Now I tell you the story of that time; a devout householder named Devidas'
Gajanan departs running like the wind, ending the incident: 'Maharaj went away swiftly, who can obstruct the wind's speed?'

scenes.brief: Devidas prepares a feast; Gajanan sits on the road eating leftover rice from discarded leaf plates, embodying 'food is Brahman'; Bankatlal witnesses this.
Bankatlal and Damodarpant debate whether Gajanan is mad or a sage; Bankatlal humbly questions him; Gajanan only gazes steadily at both.
Gajanan's radiant form described; Devidas brings a full plate of delicacies; Gajanan eats without craving; Bankatlal realizes his error, comparing Gajanan to Arjuna's feigned madness.
At midday Gajanan's gourd is empty; Damodar fetches water; Gajanan drinks from a cattle trough, then teaches worldly conduct must be followed; Damodar returns with scented water in a pot.
Gajanan teaches non-duality: water and drinker are one Brahman; both men are moved to surrender; knowing their intent, Gajanan vanishes like the wind.

unfilmed_ranges.reason: Invocations to Ganesha, Saraswati, Pandurang, Shiva, Kuladevi, Dattatreya, rishis, saints; author's humility and plea for guidance
Author urges listeners to hear saint-stories, praises saints as God on earth, source of liberation
Lists of saints from Narad to Mahipati; references to author's earlier works Bhaktivijay and Bhaktamala
Shegaon's glory described; Ramchandra Patil requests the author to write Gajanan's life during Kartiki pilgrimage
Gajanan's mysterious arrival in youth on Magh Vadya Saptami; avatar discussion citing ayonisambhava births of Nath yogis
Author announces next chapter, asks for attention, signs off with colophon and 'Shri Hari Hararpanamastu'
